logline: The morning after the storm, he walks out of the fog onto the wrecked chapel shore, says 'We can rebuild this temple', and the white temple rises with his hands until he can welcome the new day with his arms open.
reading:
A poem of aftermath turned into a building. It opens cold and quiet ('Even here is chilly in the morning'): fog rafting in over the sea, hugging the bases of the tree-covered hills, choir chords calming 'the nerves of things I can't control', and a tired flame of 'jazz tuned lyrics' that dries the dew off 'all the remnants of the destruction revealed in the sunlight'. The ruin is the storm-wrecked chapel and shattered tambourine of earlier poems, now lit plainly.

It turns on 'We can rebuild this temple. It's a new day.', his first 'we' and the 2-second silence that follows it. After the turn, the grief is still named ('the painful crawl along the cobblestone boulevards of broken dreams'), but the poem moves into the journal 'stored away from moments of great clarity', into words 'read aloud and sung alone as gospels to the lonely mirror's midnight hours' and tears drying with time. It ends with the triple 'We can embrace / receive / welcome a new day' and 'this sacred place', the world and a heart at peace. Its governing images are fog, dew, sunlight, a white temple, a journal and a mirror.
motifs: fog that hugs the bases of the hills
dew on stone, dried by sunlight
remnants of the chapel revealed in plain light
the white temple rising course by course
the journal stored away, opened and read aloud
the lonely mirror at midnight vs. the mirror-pool at morning
the triple welcome: embrace, receive, welcome
a heart at peace / still water

light_and_texture: Cold flat overcast for 11.1, built from layers of vellum and tracing paper that thin out as dawn comes. Dawn arrives as a rose-to-gold gel card sliding up behind a cut ridgeline, then hard low sun cut through slits in black card throws real raking shadows across the white temple pieces. The temple is smooth bright-white card with a matte gesso skin and visible kraft edges. The chapel rubble is torn grey board flecked with pin-dot dew. Water is a sheet of silver-grey paper under a mirrored copy of the plate.

characters.note: poet.11.action is still a blank layout: panel A ('sit · threequarter, opens the journal') and all seven hand boxes are empty brad targets, and the props row has only grey placeholder chips. The WHO column is right (Black man, faded haircut, full beard, black track jacket with red piping, sunglasses). The C style strip shows the craft well (kraft hands with brass brads, piped boots), but its seated figure wears the sunglasses painted on, which goes against the pack rule that sunglasses are a plug-in card. It lacks the palms-up guiding hand and the arms-raised pose, which this poem needs most.

fx.how: Three tracing-paper strips with feathered torn edges slide right-to-left at three speeds; under it, the arch_2723ab1b fog band as the far layer; strips thin and lift as dawn comes
Rose→gold gradient gel card rises behind a cut ridge silhouette; ambient key warms from grey to rose over 6 s (arch_0fcf01e8 Morning Mountain as reference or back layer)
Thin teased cotton or vellum curls on wires drifting slowly upward through the dawn light

Each temple piece arrives as a dot-stencil: code reveals the white card through a dot mask in 4 steps, then a tiny settle (1-frame drop) and a puff of paper dust; intercut once with arch_3b66fbdb white block models
White pin-dot dew on the rubble cards fades out dot by dot along the line of sun; reference arch_ee425236 Victory Gardens dew on leaves
Slits cut in a black card in front of the key light, with haze; rays rake the white columns. Use arch_5e2737d2 Sunburst as the far sky
Three or four four-point star cards pop on and off for 2 frames each on the new white stone
Duplicate the plate and puppet flipped below a waterline card, darkened 20% and blurred slightly, with a gentle code ripple; the archive is comped into this reflection only
A flat silver-paper disc slides under his feet and kills the ripple displacement inside its radius; it grows and shrinks with his breath
Pinholes in a blue-hour card, backlit, go out one by one from the east; or arch_1ad86700 Snow Queen stars fading
A long shadow card slides off the valley floor westward, uncovering the lit set; the temple goes grey→bone-white as it passes

passage.keep: The line choice is right: 'We can rebuild this temple' is the turn and the first 'we'. The single held palm on the coping is a builder's touch and reads as one gesture. The literal answer from Fifteen Minutes in India (1960), 'the stonework is severely plain', matches the bone-white temple, and view_052 is figure-free with a large, bright pool.
passage.better: Water reads faint, so make the reflection fill the lower 45% of frame and push the archive bright, warm-tinted and nearly full-size in the pool, edged hard by the coping card. Let it also rise into the column gaps of the portico (vertical panes read strongest), so the picture appears in the pool and the colonnade together. Swap to a head-lowered card at the hold rather than tilting, and keep his hand still for the whole answer. Start the palm descent on 'rebuild' so the contact lands on 'temple'.
alt_lines: 'I can close a chapter and open a journal stored away': hand opens the journal; the archive (National Library of Medicine 1963, arch_496e705a) opens on the open page held close to camera
'along the cobblestone boulevards of broken dreams': head lowers; Berlin Symphony cobbles (arch_ea58bcc0) open in the arched doorway of the chapel ruin (gen_e315da34f9)
'sung alone as gospels to the lonely mirror's midnight hours': palm on glass of the mirror card; the archive opens inside the mirror pane (Golden Gate City rotunda in black water, arch_62e610f9)
'We can welcome a new day': both hands open, arms up; sunrise film (arch_b9159fe6) opens between the two centre columns of the finished temple
'This world is at peace': eyes-closed head on the out-breath; THE PHOTOGRAPHER fog headland (arch_2723ab1b) opens in the chapel window slot

ideas: Arrival without a body: the headlights in gen_efa9055be2 (title text cropped) come toward camera, then cut to the motorcycle card parked small on the flats of gen_e315da34f9, with POET's back card already standing at the water
Fog that hugs: POET back card in the foreground and vellum fog strips in the middle; far layer is THE PHOTOGRAPHER 1948 headland fog (arch_2723ab1b), so the archive is the landscape he watches
Remnants in the sun: hold on gen_2bd9f63a13 (shattered tambourine under a light shaft), then the light shaft widens and the dew pin-dots on the cardboard rubble dry along it
Builder and blueprint: as his palms rise, How Our Country Grew (arch_3b66fbdb) white block models play inside the empty footprint of the platform; when it ends, the first white card course is there
Colonnade walk: he walks behind six card columns; each gap shows a beat of World of Tomorrow (arch_715f6e36) or European Trip I (arch_1a29a53f), and each column hides him for a beat
Choir chords: the robed figures walking into light in gen_8610c5199b stand as a standalone insert for 'offer them back to the higher powers' (no puppet in that frame)

Walking on water: the calm sea of Happy Wanderers (arch_b687e341) with a silver halo under his profile walk cycle; on 'mirror's midnight hours' the water darkens to Golden Gate City's black pool (arch_62e610f9)

Blue hour to sun: the finial lands under stars from The Snow Queen (arch_1ad86700); the stars go out, Rising Sun and Mountains (arch_b9159fe6) clears the cut ridge and the terminator sweep reaches his raised arms
